  5628	70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
  5629	quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix

    48	* `FreeWaveData d E` (D8): the space `E = H^{1/2} × H^{-1/2}` is an abstract real
    49	  Hilbert space; the structure carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`, group
    50	  law), the velocity reversal `𝓡` (isometric, `S_E(-h) = 𝓡 S_E(h) 𝓡`) and the
    51	  translations `τ_y`, `y ∈ ℝ^d` (isometric, commuting with every `S_E(h)`,
    52	  `⟨τ_y z, w⟩_E → 0` as `|y| → ∞`).  Each field is a property that lines 103-122 state
    53	  for the concrete objects (the weak nullity is proved there by a Riemann-Lebesgue
    54	  argument, lines 105-110; the reversal identity from the free Fourier matrix, whose
    55	  per-frequency form is `reversal_freeMatrix`; the group law per frequency is
    56	  `freeMatrix_mul`).
    57	* `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7; `P:constant-young-linear` on `𝓛(E)`, lines
    58	  91-98): along some nontrivial filter of partitions of `[s,t]` the left Young sums
    59	  converge in operator norm to `U(t,s) - I`.  The TeX's convergence as the mesh tends
    60	  to zero implies it, so it is no stronger than its source.
    61	
    62	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E ≠ 0` (`Nontrivial E`; on the zero space every
    63	operator has norm `0` and `‖S_E(h)‖ ≥ 1` fails); `d ≥ 1` (from `H:homog`'s
    64	`d ∈ {1,2,3}`; it makes the cocompact filter of `ℝ^d` nontrivial); the partition
    65	points lie in `[s,t]`.
    66	
    67	Narrower than the TeX: the operator `J_E`, the identity `ω = ⟨·, J_E ·⟩_E` with its
    68	duality form (lines 32-39, 63-68) and the preservation of `ω` by `S_E` on all of `E`
    69	(the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity, lines 82-86) are not
    70	formalized; the force claim is at the `L²` level, and the estimate
    71	`‖bu‖_{H^{-1/2}} ≤ ‖b‖_∞‖u‖_{H^{1/2}}` (line 88) is not formalized.  The Young
    72	evolution is not constructed: `U` is any operator family whose left Young sums
    73	converge (the supplied input).  The wrappers state the norm bounds and compactness
    74	claims exactly as displayed.
    75	
    76	Proof route.  As in the TeX, except: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 110-112)
    77	is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact closure of
    78	the image of a ball and the adjoint (not by subsequences), and the norm bound
    79	(lines 114-119) is proved directly for every `z` by a limit along the filter; the
    80	per-frequency symplecticity is proved through the auxiliary identity
    81	`Mᵀ J_symp M = (det M) J_symp` for every `2 × 2` matrix.  Helpers labelled auxiliary

   100	/-! ### Per-frequency free matrix -/
   101	
   102	/-- The symplectic matrix `J_symp`, `J_symp(q,p) = (p,-q)` (TeX line 64). -/
   103	def Jsymp : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ := !![0, 1; -1, 0]
   104	
   105	/-- The per-frequency symplectic form `ω₂(z,w) = z ⬝ J_symp w = z₀w₁ - z₁w₀`
   106	(balanced coordinates `z = (q,p)`). -/
   107	def omega2 (z w : Fin 2 → ℝ) : ℝ := z ⬝ᵥ (Jsymp *ᵥ w)
   108	
   109	/-- Auxiliary: the coordinate form of `ω₂`. -/
   110	theorem omega2_eq (z w : Fin 2 → ℝ) : omega2 z w = z 0 * w 1 - z 1 * w 0 := by
   111	  simp [omega2, Jsymp, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two]
   112	  ring
   113	
   114	/-- Auxiliary (Lean route): for every real `2 × 2` matrix,
   115	`Mᵀ J_symp M = (det M) J_symp`. -/
   116	theorem transpose_mul_Jsymp_mul (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) :
   117	    Mᵀ * Jsymp * M = M.det • Jsymp := by
   118	  ext i j
   119	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
   120	    simp [Jsymp, Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.det_fin_two] <;> ring
   121	
   122	/-- Auxiliary (Lean route): `ω₂(Mz, Mw) = (det M) ω₂(z,w)`. -/
   123	theorem omega2_mulVec (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) (z w : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
   124	    omega2 (M *ᵥ z) (M *ᵥ w) = M.det * omega2 z w := by
   125	  simp only [omega2_eq, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.det_fin_two]
   126	  ring
   127	
   128	/-- The continuous sine quotient `t ↦ sin(tk)/k`, with value `t` at `k = 0`:
   129	`sineQuotient t k = t · sinc(tk)`. -/
   130	def sineQuotient (t k : ℝ) : ℝ := t * Real.sinc (t * k)
   131	
   132	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t k = sin(tk)/k` for `k ≠ 0`. -/
   133	theorem sineQuotient_of_ne_zero (t : ℝ) {k : ℝ} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
   134	    sineQuotient t k = Real.sin (t * k) / k := by
   135	  unfold sineQuotient
   136	  by_cases ht : t = 0
   137	  · simp [ht]
   138	  · rw [Real.sinc_of_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero ht hk)]
   139	    field_simp
   140	
   141	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t 0 = t`. -/
   142	theorem sineQuotient_zero (t : ℝ) : sineQuotient t 0 = t := by
   143	  simp [sineQuotient]
   144	
   145	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t k · k = sin(tk)`, every `k`. -/
   146	theorem sineQuotient_mul (t k : ℝ) : sineQuotient t k * k = Real.sin (t * k) := by
   147	  by_cases hk : k = 0
   148	  · simp [hk]
   149	  · rw [sineQuotient_of_ne_zero t hk]
   150	    field_simp
   151	
   152	/-- The sine quotient is continuous in `k` (the "continuous sine quotient", line 79). -/
   153	theorem continuous_sineQuotient (t : ℝ) : Continuous (fun k => sineQuotient t k) := by
   154	  unfold sineQuotient
   155	  fun_prop
   156	
   157	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient (-t) k = -sineQuotient t k`. -/
   158	theorem sineQuotient_neg (t k : ℝ) : sineQuotient (-t) k = -sineQuotient t k := by
   159	  simp [sineQuotient, neg_mul, Real.sinc_neg]
   160	
   161	/-- The free matrix in balanced Fourier coordinates (TeX lines 70-77), with
   162	frequency modulus `k = |ξ|` and weight `br = ⟨ξ⟩`; the `(0,1)` entry uses
   163	the continuous sine quotient, so the matrix at `k = 0` is the TeX's limit. -/
   164	def freeMatrix (t k br : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
   165	  !![Real.cos (t * k), br * sineQuotient t k; -(k * Real.sin (t * k)) / br, Real.cos (t * k)]
   166	
   167	/-- The free matrix at the frequency `ξ ∈ ℝ^d`: `k = |ξ|`, `⟨ξ⟩ = √(1+|ξ|²)`. -/
   168	def freeMatrixAt {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
   169	  freeMatrix t ‖ξ‖ (Real.sqrt (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2))
   170	
   171	/-- Auxiliary: `⟨ξ⟩ = √(1+|ξ|²) > 0`. -/
   172	theorem bracket_pos {d : ℕ} (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : 0 < Real.sqrt (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) :=
   173	  Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
   174	
   175	/-- At nonzero frequency the free matrix is the B22 matrix
   176	`DimensionalMatrix.forward (cos tk) (sin tk) (k/⟨ξ⟩)`. -/
   177	theorem freeMatrix_eq_forward (t : ℝ) {k br : ℝ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   178	    freeMatrix t k br =
   179	      StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward (Real.cos (t * k)) (Real.sin (t * k))
   180	        (k / br) := by
   181	  rw [freeMatrix, StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward,
   182	    sineQuotient_of_ne_zero t hk]
   183	  ext i j
   184	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp <;> field_simp
   185	
   186	/-- At frequency zero the free matrix is `!![1, br t; 0, 1]` (TeX line 78 with `⟨0⟩ = 1`). -/
   187	theorem freeMatrix_zero_freq (t br : ℝ) : freeMatrix t 0 br = !![1, br * t; 0, 1] := by
   188	  simp [freeMatrix, sineQuotient_zero]
   189	
   190	/-- `W_t(0) = (1 t; 0 1)` (TeX line 78). -/
   191	theorem freeMatrixAt_zero {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) :
   192	    freeMatrixAt t (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) = !![1, t; 0, 1] := by
   193	  simp [freeMatrixAt, freeMatrix_zero_freq]
   194	
   195	/-- The entries of the free matrix are continuous in the frequency modulus `k`
   196	(fixed `t` and `br`), the frequency-zero value included. -/
   197	theorem continuous_freeMatrix (t br : ℝ) :
   198	    Continuous (fun k => freeMatrix t k br) := by
   199	  refine continuous_pi fun i => continuous_pi fun j => ?_
   200	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [freeMatrix]
   201	  · fun_prop
   202	  · exact continuous_const.mul (continuous_sineQuotient t)
   203	  · fun_prop
   204	  · fun_prop
   205	
   206	/-- Determinant one at every frequency, also at zero (TeX lines 80-81). -/
   207	theorem det_freeMatrix (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) : (freeMatrix t k br).det = 1 := by
   208	  rw [Matrix.det_fin_two]
   209	  simp only [freeMatrix, Matrix.of_apply, Matrix.cons_val', Matrix.cons_val_zero,
   210	    Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.empty_val', Matrix.cons_val_fin_one]
   211	  have h1 := sineQuotient_mul t k
   212	  have h2 : br * sineQuotient t k * (-(k * Real.sin (t * k)) / br)
   213	      = -(sineQuotient t k * k) * Real.sin (t * k) := by
   214	    field_simp
   215	  rw [h2, h1]
   216	  nlinarith [Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (t * k)]
   217	
   218	/-- Per-frequency symplecticity `W_tᵀ J_symp W_t = J_symp` (TeX lines 79-81), at
   219	every frequency modulus `k`, zero included, for every weight `br ≠ 0`. -/
   220	theorem freeMatrix_symplectic (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   221	    (freeMatrix t k br)ᵀ * Jsymp * freeMatrix t k br = Jsymp := by
   222	  rw [transpose_mul_Jsymp_mul, det_freeMatrix t k hbr, one_smul]
   223	
   224	/-- `W_t(ξ)ᵀ J_symp W_t(ξ) = J_symp` at every `ξ ∈ ℝ^d`, `ξ = 0` included. -/
   225	theorem freeMatrixAt_symplectic {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
   226	    (freeMatrixAt t ξ)ᵀ * Jsymp * freeMatrixAt t ξ = Jsymp :=
   227	  freeMatrix_symplectic t ‖ξ‖ (bracket_pos ξ).ne'
   228	
   229	/-- The free matrix preserves the per-frequency form: `ω₂(W_t z, W_t w) = ω₂(z,w)`. -/
   230	theorem freeMatrix_preserves_omega2 (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) (z w : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
   231	    omega2 (freeMatrix t k br *ᵥ z) (freeMatrix t k br *ᵥ w) = omega2 z w := by
   232	  rw [omega2_mulVec, det_freeMatrix t k hbr, one_mul]
   233	
   234	/-- Per-frequency group law `W_s W_t = W_{s+t}` (the frequency form of the group law of
   235	the free group used in TeX lines 101 and 121-122). -/
   236	theorem freeMatrix_mul (s t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   237	    freeMatrix s k br * freeMatrix t k br = freeMatrix (s + t) k br := by
   238	  by_cases hk : k = 0
   239	  · subst hk
   240	    simp only [freeMatrix_zero_freq]
   241	    ext i j
   242	    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two]
   243	    ring
   244	  · simp only [freeMatrix, sineQuotient_of_ne_zero _ hk]
   245	    ext i j
   246	    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
   247	      simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two, add_mul, Real.cos_add, Real.sin_add] <;>
   248	      field_simp <;> ring
   249	
   250	/-- The velocity reversal `diag(1,-1)`. -/
   251	def reversal : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ := !![1, 0; 0, -1]
   252	
   253	/-- Per-frequency reversal identity `R W_t R = W_{-t}` (TeX lines 120-121). -/
   254	theorem reversal_freeMatrix (t k br : ℝ) :
   255	    reversal * freeMatrix t k br * reversal = freeMatrix (-t) k br := by
   256	  ext i j
   257	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
   258	    simp [reversal, freeMatrix, Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two, sineQuotient_neg,
   259	      neg_mul, Real.cos_neg, Real.sin_neg, neg_div]
   260

261	/-! ### Skewness of the force for the symplectic form -/
   262	
   263	section Force
   264	
   265	variable {U V : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module ℝ U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V]
   266	
   267	/-- The symplectic form `ω((u,v),(f,g)) = P(u,g) - P(f,v)` for a pairing
   268	`P : U × V → ℝ` (TeX line 36, with `P` the `H^{1/2}`-`H^{-1/2}` duality). -/
   269	def omega (P : U →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (z w : U × V) : ℝ := P z.1 w.2 - P w.1 z.2
   270	
   271	/-- The force `B(b)(u,v) = (0, M u)` for a map `M : U → V` (TeX line 41 with
   272	`M u = b u`). -/
   273	def force (M : U → V) (z : U × V) : U × V := (0, M z.1)
   274	
   275	/-- Skewness of the force for `ω`: if the pairing is symmetric through `M`
   276	(`P(f, Mu) = P(u, Mf)`), then `ω(B z, w) + ω(z, B w) = 0` (TeX lines 40-41 and
   277	88-91). -/
   278	theorem omega_force_skew (P : U →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (M : U → V)
   279	    (hsymm : ∀ u f : U, P f (M u) = P u (M f)) (z w : U × V) :
   280	    omega P (force M z) w + omega P z (force M w) = 0 := by
   281	  simp [omega, force, hsymm z.1 w.1]
   282	
   283	end Force
   284	
   285	section ForceL2
   286	
   287	variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure X)
   288	
   289	/-- The `L²` form `ω((u,v),(f,g)) = ∫ u g - ∫ f v` on pairs of real functions
   290	(the balanced `L²` pairing of TeX lines 67 and 89-90). -/
   291	def omegaL2 (z w : (X → ℝ) × (X → ℝ)) : ℝ :=
   292	  (∫ x, z.1 x * w.2 x ∂μ) - ∫ x, w.1 x * z.2 x ∂μ
   293	
   294	/-- The force `B(b)(u,v) = (0, b u)` on pairs of real functions. -/
   295	def forceL2 (b : X → ℝ) (z : (X → ℝ) × (X → ℝ)) : (X → ℝ) × (X → ℝ) :=
   296	  (0, fun x => b x * z.1 x)
   297	
   298	/-- Skewness at the `L²` level: `ω(B(b)z,w) + ω(z,B(b)w) = -∫ f b u + ∫ u b f = 0`
   299	(TeX lines 89-91). -/
   300	theorem omegaL2_force_skew (b : X → ℝ) (z w : (X → ℝ) × (X → ℝ)) :
   301	    omegaL2 μ (forceL2 b z) w + omegaL2 μ z (forceL2 b w) = 0 := by
   302	  simp only [omegaL2, forceL2, Pi.zero_apply, zero_mul, MeasureTheory.integral_zero, sub_zero,
   303	    zero_sub]
   304	  have : (fun x => w.1 x * (b x * z.1 x)) = fun x => z.1 x * (b x * w.1 x) := by
   305	    funext x; ring
   306	  rw [this]
   307	  ring
   308	
   309	/-- The cancellation of TeX lines 89-90 is absolutely integrable: for `u, f ∈ L²`
   310	and a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable `b`, the integrand `f (b u)` is integrable. -/
   311	theorem integrable_mul_force (b u f : X → ℝ) (C : ℝ) (hb : MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable b μ)
   312	    (hbC : ∀ x, |b x| ≤ C) (hu : MeasureTheory.MemLp u 2 μ) (hf : MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 μ) :
   313	    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => f x * (b x * u x)) μ := by
   314	  have hbu : MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => b x * u x) 2 μ := by
   315	    refine MeasureTheory.MemLp.of_le_mul (c := C) hu (hb.mul hu.aestronglyMeasurable) ?_
   316	    refine Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_
   317	    simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul]
   318	    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hbC x) (abs_nonneg _)
   319	  exact hf.integrable_mul hbu
   320	
   321	end ForceL2

   323	/-! ### Compact operators -/
   324	
   325	section Compact
   326	
   327	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   328	
   329	/-- Auxiliary: a bounded operator after a compact one is compact. -/
   330	theorem isCompactOperator_mul_left (A : E →L[ℝ] E) {K : E →L[ℝ] E}
   331	    (hK : IsCompactOperator K) : IsCompactOperator (A * K) := by
   332	  have : ⇑(A * K) = A ∘ K := rfl
   333	  rw [this]
   334	  exact hK.clm_comp A
   335	
   336	/-- Auxiliary: a compact operator after a bounded one is compact. -/
   337	theorem isCompactOperator_mul_right {K : E →L[ℝ] E} (hK : IsCompactOperator K)
   338	    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) : IsCompactOperator (K * A) := by
   339	  have : ⇑(K * A) = K ∘ A := rfl
   340	  rw [this]
   341	  exact hK.comp_clm A
   342	
   343	/-- Auxiliary: differences of compact operators are compact (operator form). -/
   344	theorem isCompactOperator_sub' {A B : E →L[ℝ] E} (hA : IsCompactOperator A)
   345	    (hB : IsCompactOperator B) : IsCompactOperator (A - B) := by
   346	  have : ⇑(A - B) = ⇑A - ⇑B := rfl
   347	  rw [this]
   348	  exact hA.sub hB
   349	
   350	/-- Auxiliary: sums of compact operators are compact (operator form). -/
   351	theorem isCompactOperator_add' {A B : E →L[ℝ] E} (hA : IsCompactOperator A)
   352	    (hB : IsCompactOperator B) : IsCompactOperator (A + B) := by
   353	  have : ⇑(A + B) = ⇑A + ⇑B := rfl
   354	  rw [this]
   355	  exact hA.add hB
   356	
   357	/-- Closedness of the compact ideal: a norm limit, along a nontrivial filter, of
   358	operators that are eventually compact is compact (TeX lines 98-99). -/
   359	theorem isCompactOperator_of_tendsto [CompleteSpace E] {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot]
   360	    {A : ι → E →L[ℝ] E} {B : E →L[ℝ] E} (hlim : Tendsto A l (𝓝 B))
   361	    (hA : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsCompactOperator (A i)) : IsCompactOperator B :=
   362	  isClosed_setOfPred_isCompactOperator.mem_of_tendsto hlim hA
   363	
   364	/-- The left Young sum `∑_{j<n} (X(p_{j+1}) - X(p_j)) U(p_j, s)` (TeX lines 95-97). -/
   365	def youngSum (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s : ℝ) (p : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
   366	    E →L[ℝ] E :=
   367	  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (X (p (j + 1)) - X (p j)) * U (p j) s
   368	
   369	/-- Each left Young sum is compact when `X` is compact at the partition points
   370	(TeX lines 94-98). -/
   371	theorem isCompactOperator_youngSum (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s : ℝ)
   372	    (p : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hX : ∀ j ≤ n, IsCompactOperator (X (p j))) :
   373	    IsCompactOperator (youngSum X U s p n) := by
   374	  unfold youngSum
   375	  refine Finset.sum_induction _ (fun A : E →L[ℝ] E => IsCompactOperator A)
   376	    (fun A B hA hB => isCompactOperator_add' hA hB) isCompactOperator_zero ?_
   377	  intro j hj
   378	  have hj' := Finset.mem_range.1 hj
   379	  exact isCompactOperator_mul_right
   380	    (isCompactOperator_sub' (hX (j + 1) (by omega)) (hX j (by omega))) _
   381	
   382	/-- The ordered product `P_N ⋯ P_0`. -/
   383	def orderedProd (P : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E) : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E
   384	  | 0 => P 0
   385	  | n + 1 => P (n + 1) * orderedProd P n
   386	
   387	/-- Telescoping (TeX lines 125-128): if every `P_j - Q_j`, `j ≤ N`, is compact, then
   388	`P_N ⋯ P_0 - Q_N ⋯ Q_0` is compact. -/
   389	theorem isCompactOperator_orderedProd_sub (P Q : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E) (N : ℕ)
   390	    (h : ∀ j ≤ N, IsCompactOperator (P j - Q j)) :
   391	    IsCompactOperator (orderedProd P N - orderedProd Q N) := by
   392	  induction N with
   393	  | zero => simpa [orderedProd] using h 0 le_rfl
   394	  | succ n ih =>
   395	    have hdecomp : orderedProd P (n + 1) - orderedProd Q (n + 1)
   396	        = (P (n + 1) - Q (n + 1)) * orderedProd P n
   397	          + Q (n + 1) * (orderedProd P n - orderedProd Q n) := by
   398	      simp only [orderedProd, sub_mul, mul_sub]
   399	      abel
   400	    rw [hdecomp]
   401	    exact isCompactOperator_add'
   402	      (isCompactOperator_mul_right (h (n + 1) le_rfl) _)
   403	      (isCompactOperator_mul_left _ (ih fun j hj => h j (by omega)))
   404

   409	section Hilbert

   411	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

   413	/-- Weak nullity of a family along a filter: `⟨x_i, w⟩ → 0` for every `w`. -/
   414	def WeaklyNull {ι : Type*} (l : Filter ι) (x : ι → E) : Prop :=
   415	  ∀ w : E, Tendsto (fun i => inner ℝ (x i) w) l (𝓝 0)
   416	
   417	omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] in
   418	/-- Auxiliary: a cluster point of `f` along `l` at which `g ∘ f → 0` for a continuous `g`
   419	has `g = 0` there. -/
   420	theorem eq_zero_of_mapClusterPt {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {f : ι → E} {p : E}
   421	    {g : E → ℝ} (hg : Continuous g) (hp : MapClusterPt p l f)
   422	    (hlim : Tendsto (g ∘ f) l (𝓝 0)) : g p = 0 := by
   423	  have hc : MapClusterPt (g p) l (g ∘ f) := hp.continuousAt_comp hg.continuousAt
   424	  by_contra hne
   425	  have hdis : Disjoint (𝓝 (g p)) (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)) := disjoint_nhds_nhds.2 hne
   426	  have hle : 𝓝 (g p) ⊓ Filter.map (g ∘ f) l ≤ ⊥ :=
   427	    (inf_le_inf_left _ hlim).trans hdis.le_bot
   428	  exact (hc.neBot).ne (le_bot_iff.1 hle)
   429	
   430	/-- A compact operator maps a bounded weakly null family (along any filter) to a norm
   431	null family (TeX lines 110-112; the Lean route uses cluster points in the compact
   432	closure of the image of a ball, not subsequences). -/
   433	theorem tendsto_compact_of_weaklyNull {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} (K : E →L[ℝ] E)
   434	    (hK : IsCompactOperator K) (x : ι → E) (C : ℝ) (hb : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ C)
   435	    (hw : WeaklyNull l x) : Tendsto (fun i => K (x i)) l (𝓝 0) := by
   436	  have hcpt : IsCompact (closure (K '' Metric.closedBall (0 : E) C)) :=
   437	    hK.isCompact_closure_image_of_bounded Metric.isBounded_closedBall
   438	  refine hcpt.tendsto_nhds_of_unique_mapClusterPt
   439	    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun i => subset_closure ⟨x i, by simpa using hb i, rfl⟩) ?_
   440	  intro p _ hp
   441	  have hlim : Tendsto ((fun q : E => inner ℝ q p) ∘ fun i => K (x i)) l (𝓝 0) := by
   442	    have := hw (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint K p)
   443	    refine this.congr fun i => ?_
   444	    simp [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
   445	  have h0 := eq_zero_of_mapClusterPt (continuous_id.inner continuous_const) hp hlim
   446	  simpa using h0
   447	
   448	/-- Abstract compact-perturbation bound (TeX lines 103-119): if `S` commutes with
   449	isometries `τ_i` such that `τ_i z` is weakly null along a nontrivial filter for every
   450	`z`, then `‖S‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖` for every compact `K`. -/
   451	theorem norm_le_norm_add_compact {ι : Type*} (l : Filter ι) [l.NeBot] (S : E →L[ℝ] E)
   452	    (τ : ι → E →L[ℝ] E) (hiso : ∀ i z, ‖τ i z‖ = ‖z‖) (hcomm : ∀ i, S * τ i = τ i * S)
   453	    (hnull : ∀ z, WeaklyNull l (fun i => τ i z)) (K : E →L[ℝ] E) (hK : IsCompactOperator K) :
   454	    ‖S‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖ := by
   455	  refine ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (norm_nonneg _) fun z => ?_
   456	  have hKt : Tendsto (fun i => ‖K (τ i z)‖) l (𝓝 0) := by
   457	    have := tendsto_compact_of_weaklyNull K hK (fun i => τ i z) ‖z‖
   458	      (fun i => (hiso i z).le) (hnull z)
   459	    simpa using this.norm
   460	  have hpt : ∀ i, ‖S z‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖ * ‖z‖ + ‖K (τ i z)‖ := by
   461	    intro i
   462	    have h1 : ‖S z‖ = ‖S (τ i z)‖ := by
   463	      have : S (τ i z) = τ i (S z) := by
   464	        simpa using congrArg (fun A : E →L[ℝ] E => A z) (hcomm i)
   465	      rw [this, hiso]
   466	    have h2 : S (τ i z) = (S + K) (τ i z) - K (τ i z) := by simp
   467	    rw [h1, h2]
   468	    refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ?_
   469	    gcongr
   470	    calc ‖(S + K) (τ i z)‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖ * ‖τ i z‖ := ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm _ _
   471	      _ = ‖S + K‖ * ‖z‖ := by rw [hiso]
   472	  have hlim : Tendsto (fun i => ‖S + K‖ * ‖z‖ + ‖K (τ i z)‖) l (𝓝 (‖S + K‖ * ‖z‖ + 0)) :=
   473	    tendsto_const_nhds.add hKt
   474	  rw [add_zero] at hlim
   475	  exact ge_of_tendsto hlim (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hpt)
   476	
   477	/-- Corollary: `‖S‖ ≤ ‖A‖` whenever `A - S` is compact (same hypotheses on `S`). -/
   478	theorem norm_le_of_sub_compact {ι : Type*} (l : Filter ι) [l.NeBot] (S A : E →L[ℝ] E)
   479	    (τ : ι → E →L[ℝ] E) (hiso : ∀ i z, ‖τ i z‖ = ‖z‖) (hcomm : ∀ i, S * τ i = τ i * S)
   480	    (hnull : ∀ z, WeaklyNull l (fun i => τ i z)) (hK : IsCompactOperator (A - S)) :
   481	    ‖S‖ ≤ ‖A‖ := by
   482	  have := norm_le_norm_add_compact l S τ hiso hcomm hnull (A - S) hK
   483	  simpa using this
   484	
   485	end Hilbert

   487	/-! ### Norm at least one from the group law and the reversal -/
   488	
   489	section NormOne
   490	
   491	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   492	
   493	/-- If `B A = I`, `B = R A R` and `R` is an isometry, then `1 ≤ ‖A‖` (TeX lines
   494	120-122).  `Nontrivial E` is needed: on the zero space every operator has norm zero. -/
   495	theorem one_le_norm_of_reversal [Nontrivial E] (A B R : E →L[ℝ] E) (hBA : B * A = 1)
   496	    (hR : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖) (hB : B = R * A * R) : 1 ≤ ‖A‖ := by
   497	  have hRn : ‖R‖ ≤ 1 :=
   498	    ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ zero_le_one fun z => by rw [hR, one_mul]
   499	  have hBn : ‖B‖ ≤ ‖A‖ := by
   500	    rw [hB]
   501	    calc ‖R * A * R‖ ≤ ‖R * A‖ * ‖R‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
   502	      _ ≤ (‖R‖ * ‖A‖) * ‖R‖ := by gcongr; exact norm_mul_le _ _
   503	      _ ≤ (1 * ‖A‖) * 1 := by gcongr
   504	      _ = ‖A‖ := by ring
   505	  have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖A‖ := by
   506	    calc (1 : ℝ) = ‖(1 : E →L[ℝ] E)‖ := norm_one.symm
   507	      _ = ‖B * A‖ := by rw [hBA]
   508	      _ ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖A‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
   509	  have hA0 : 0 ≤ ‖A‖ := norm_nonneg _
   510	  nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hBn hA0]
   511	
   512	end NormOne

   514	/-! ### Supplied inputs and the wrappers -/
   515	
   516	/-- Supplied input (D8; TeX lines 103-122): the free wave group `S_E` on
   517	`E = H^{1/2} × H^{-1/2}`, the velocity reversal `𝓡(u,v) = (u,-v)` and the spatial
   518	translations `τ_y`, `y ∈ ℝ^d`, with the properties the proof of `L:symplectic-free`
   519	states for them: the group law, `S_E(-h) = 𝓡 S_E(h) 𝓡` with `𝓡` isometric,
   520	translations isometric and commuting with `S_E(h)`, and `⟨τ_y z, w⟩_E → 0` as

521	`|y| → ∞` (cocompact filter on `ℝ^d`). -/
   522	structure FreeWaveData (d : ℕ) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where
   523	  /-- The free group `S_E(t)`. -/
   524	  S : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E
   525	  S_zero : S 0 = 1
   526	  S_add : ∀ s t, S (s + t) = S s * S t
   527	  /-- The velocity reversal. -/
   528	  R : E →L[ℝ] E
   529	  R_norm : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖
   530	  S_neg : ∀ h, S (-h) = R * S h * R
   531	  /-- The translations `τ_y`. -/
   532	  τ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → E →L[ℝ] E
   533	  τ_norm : ∀ y z, ‖τ y z‖ = ‖z‖
   534	  τ_comm : ∀ y h, S h * τ y = τ y * S h
   535	  τ_weak : ∀ z w, Tendsto (fun y => inner ℝ (τ y z) w) (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (𝓝 0)
   536	
   537	/-- Supplied input (D7; `P:constant-young-linear` on `𝓛(E)`, TeX lines 91-98): the left
   538	Young sums of `X` over partitions of `[s,t]` converge in operator norm to
   539	`U(t,s) - I` along some nontrivial filter of partitions.  A partition is a pair
   540	`(n, p)` with points `p 0, …, p n`; only the points `p j`, `j ≤ n`, enter, and they lie
   541	in `[s,t]` eventually.  The TeX's convergence as the mesh tends to zero implies this
   542	statement (the mesh filter is nontrivial). -/
   543	def LeftYoungSumsConverge {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   544	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s t : ℝ) : Prop :=
   545	  ∃ l : Filter (ℕ × (ℕ → ℝ)), l.NeBot ∧
   546	    (∀ᶠ π in l, ∀ j ≤ π.1, π.2 j ∈ Set.Icc s t) ∧
   547	    Tendsto (fun π => youngSum X U s π.2 π.1) l (𝓝 (U t s - 1))
   548	
   549	section Wrappers
   550	
   551	variable {d : ℕ} {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
   552	
   553	/-- Auxiliary: for `d ≥ 1` the cocompact filter of `ℝ^d` is nontrivial. -/
   554	theorem FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
   555	    (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))).NeBot := by
   556	  have : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
   557	  infer_instance
   558	
   559	omit [CompleteSpace E] in
   560	/-- `‖S_E(h)‖ ≥ 1` (TeX lines 120-122), for a nonzero `E`. -/
   561	theorem FreeWaveData.one_le_norm [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (h : ℝ) :
   562	    1 ≤ ‖F.S h‖ :=
   563	  one_le_norm_of_reversal (F.S h) (F.S (-h)) F.R
   564	    (by rw [← F.S_add, neg_add_cancel, F.S_zero]) F.R_norm (F.S_neg h)
   565	
   566	/-- `‖S_E(h)‖ ≤ ‖S_E(h) + K‖` for every compact `K` (TeX lines 103-119), `d ≥ 1`. -/
   567	theorem FreeWaveData.norm_le_norm_add_compact (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (h : ℝ)
   568	    (K : E →L[ℝ] E) (hK : IsCompactOperator K) : ‖F.S h‖ ≤ ‖F.S h + K‖ := by
   569	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   570	  exact SymplecticFree.norm_le_norm_add_compact (cocompact _) (F.S h) F.τ F.τ_norm
   571	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y h) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) K hK
   572	
   573	/-- The compact Young baseline in general form: if the left Young sums of `X` over
   574	partitions of `[s,t]` converge to `U(t,s) - I` (supplied, D7) and `X` is compact on
   575	`[s,t]`, then `U(t,s) - I` and `S_E(t) U(t,s) S_E(-s) - S_E(t-s)` are compact, and
   576	`‖S_E(t) U(t,s) S_E(-s)‖ ≥ ‖S_E(t-s)‖ ≥ 1`. -/
   577	theorem compact_young_baseline [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
   578	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s t : ℝ)
   579	    (hXK : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, IsCompactOperator (X r))
   580	    (hY : LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t) :
   581	    IsCompactOperator ⇑(U t s - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E) ∧
   582	      IsCompactOperator (F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s)) ∧
   583	      ‖F.S (t - s)‖ ≤ ‖F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s)‖ ∧ 1 ≤ ‖F.S (t - s)‖ := by
   584	  obtain ⟨l, hl, hpts, hlim⟩ := hY
   585	  have hU : IsCompactOperator ⇑(U t s - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E) := by
   586	    refine isCompactOperator_of_tendsto hlim ?_
   587	    filter_upwards [hpts] with π hπ
   588	    exact isCompactOperator_youngSum X U s π.2 π.1 fun j hj => hXK _ (hπ j hj)
   589	  have hdiff : F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s) = F.S t * (U t s - 1) * F.S (-s) := by
   590	    rw [sub_eq_add_neg t s, F.S_add, mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_one]
   591	  have hK : IsCompactOperator (F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s)) := by
   592	    rw [hdiff]
   593	    exact isCompactOperator_mul_right (isCompactOperator_mul_left _ hU) _
   594	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   595	  refine ⟨hU, hK, ?_, F.one_le_norm _⟩
   596	  exact norm_le_of_sub_compact (cocompact _) (F.S (t - s)) _ F.τ F.τ_norm
   597	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y _) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) hK
   598	
   599	omit [CompleteSpace E] in
   600	/-- Auxiliary: the free product `S_E(ℓ_N) ⋯ S_E(ℓ_0) = S_E(∑_{j ≤ N} ℓ_j)` (group law). -/
   601	theorem FreeWaveData.orderedProd_S (F : FreeWaveData d E) (ℓ : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
   602	    orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j)) N = F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j) := by
   603	  induction N with
   604	  | zero => simp [orderedProd]
   605	  | succ n ih =>
   606	    rw [orderedProd, ih, ← F.S_add]
   607	    congr 1
   608	    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ _ (n + 1)]
   609	    ring
   610	
   611	/-- The compact product baseline in general form: if each `U_j(ℓ_j,0) - I` is compact,
   612	`P_j = S_E(ℓ_j) U_j(ℓ_j,0)`, then `P_N ⋯ P_0 - S_E(∑ ℓ_j)` is compact and
   613	`‖P_N ⋯ P_0‖ ≥ ‖S_E(∑ ℓ_j)‖ ≥ 1`. -/
   614	theorem compact_product_baseline [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
   615	    (U : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (ℓ : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ)
   616	    (hU : ∀ j ≤ N, IsCompactOperator ⇑(U j (ℓ j) 0 - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E)) :
   617	    IsCompactOperator (orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N
   618	        - F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)) ∧
   619	      ‖F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)‖
   620	        ≤ ‖orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N‖ ∧
   621	      1 ≤ ‖F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)‖ := by
   622	  have hK : IsCompactOperator (orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N
   623	      - F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)) := by
   624	    rw [← F.orderedProd_S ℓ N]
   625	    refine isCompactOperator_orderedProd_sub _ _ N fun j hj => ?_
   626	    have : F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0 - F.S (ℓ j) = F.S (ℓ j) * (U j (ℓ j) 0 - 1) := by
   627	      rw [mul_sub, mul_one]
   628	    rw [this]
   629	    exact isCompactOperator_mul_left _ (hU j hj)
   630	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   631	  refine ⟨hK, ?_, F.one_le_norm _⟩
   632	  exact norm_le_of_sub_compact (cocompact _) _ _ F.τ F.τ_norm
   633	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y _) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) hK

   661	    (T : ℝ) (_hT : 0 < T) (θ : ℝ≥0) (_hθ : 1 / 2 < θ) (_hθ1 : θ < 1)
   662	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (CX : ℝ≥0) (_hXhol : HolderOnWith CX θ X (Set.Icc 0 T))

   679	Young inputs.  Carried, unused (hypotheses of the supplied Young input): `θ`, the

   681	theorem symplectic_compact_product_baseline_paper [Nontrivial E]
   682	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (F : FreeWaveData d E)
   683	    (B : ℝ) (θ : ℝ≥0) (_hθ : 1 / 2 < θ) (_hθ1 : θ < 1) (N : ℕ)
   684	    (X : ℕ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (CX : ℕ → ℝ≥0)
   685	    (_hXhol : ∀ j ≤ N, HolderOnWith (CX j) θ (X j) (Set.Icc 0 B))

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=

    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=

    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re

    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:

    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=

    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ

1	\section{The symplectic form and mean evolution on time blocks}
     2	\label{S:actual-symplectic-phase}
     3	
     4	Retain the original model, covariance amplitude, physical mask $m_R$ and real $E
     5	= H^{1/2}\times H^{-1/2}$. Fix finite $R,T > 0$ and admissible exponents as
     6	in~\eqref{E:driver-parameters}. Let $M = M_R(W)$ be the from the given noise
     7	first interaction path on $E$, and $M^\rho$ its regularized paths from
     8	Proposition~\ref{P:source-gaussian-transfer} and the source construction. Here
     9	$\rho$ is the positive heat/Laplace smoothing pair. The construction preserving
    10	the given noise and ordinary rows are those of
    11	Lemma~\ref{L:source-retaining-isometry},
    12	Lemma~\ref{L:source-pointfield-regularity} and
    13	Proposition~\ref{P:source-ordinary-response}. The full $F$ operator path and
    14	Young evolution are fixed by Proposition~\ref{P:constant-phase-driver} and
    15	Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear}; their $E$ restrictions are used here.
    16	Complexifications commute with conjugation, so these real restrictions are the
    17	physical phases. For fixed $\Phi$ in the full positive-time original $H_W$ and
    18	real $c$ set
    19	\begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-combined-driver}
    20	  \begin{aligned}
    21	    Z&=W(\Phi),\qquad D_\Phi=\E[ZM],\qquad
    22	    D_\Phi^\rho=\E[ZM^\rho],\\
    23	    D&=cM+D_\Phi,\qquad D^\rho=cM^\rho+D_\Phi^\rho .
    24	  \end{aligned}
    25	\end{equation}
    26	All these are operator paths on $E$. The covariance mean is not a pointwise
    27	original potential. Write $U_D$ for left Young evolution and $P_D(t,s) =
    28	S_E(t)U_D(t,s)S_E(-s)$.
    29	
    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
    64	  onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
    65	  $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
    66	  operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
    67	  displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
    68	  of a general distributional velocity is taken.
    69	
    70	  In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
    71	  \[
    72	    W_t(\xi)=
    73	    \begin{pmatrix}
    74	      \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
    75	      -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
    76	    \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
    77	  \]
    78	  At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
    79	  the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
    80	  $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
    81	  $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
    84	  Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
    85	  Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
    86	  generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
    87	
    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
    89	  Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
    90	  $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
    91	  Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
    93	  proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
    94	  $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
    95	  \[
    96	    \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
    97	  \]
    98	  is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
    99	  of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   100	  in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   101	  that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   102	
   103	  We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   104	  Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   105	  $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   106	  transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   107	  integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   108	  function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by
   109	  parts for the approximants, proves $\langle\tau_yz,w\rangle_E \to 0$ as $|y|
   110	  \to \infty$. Thus, $\tau_yz$ tends weakly to zero. For compact $K$,
   111	  $\|K\tau_yz\| \to 0$: otherwise compactness supplies a norm-convergent
   112	  subsequence with nonzero norm, while bounded linear testing makes its limit
   113	  zero. For unit $z$ it follows that
   114	  \[
   115	    \|S_E(h)+K\|
   116	    \ge\liminf_{|y|\to\infty}\|(S_E(h)+K)\tau_yz\|
   117	    \ge\|S_E(h)z\|.
   118	  \]
   119	  Taking the supremum over $z$ gives $\|S_E(h)+K\| \ge \|S_E(h)\|$. The
   120	  isometric velocity reversal $\mathcal{R}(u,v) = (u,-v)$ satisfies $S_E(-h) =
   121	  \mathcal{R} S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$ by the full free Fourier matrix. The group law
   122	  yields $1 \le \|S_E(-h)\|\|S_E(h)\| = \|S_E(h)\|^2$. This
   123	  proves~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}.
   124	
   125	  Finally, $P_j-S_E(\ell_j)$ is compact. Telescoping the finite ordered product
   126	  against its free product gives a finite sum of bounded--compact--bounded
   127	  products, hence a compact difference. Only the free factors are combined by
   128	  the group law; no noisy factors are commuted. The same translation argument
   129	  proves \eqref{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}. A zero length gives $P_j
   130	  = I$. All assertions are at fixed finite horizons and products; no uniform
   131	  compact approximation in a radius, horizon or number of factors is asserted.
   132	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:symplectic-free}.
   133	\end{proof}

   142	  \end{equation}

    27	  195|   \end{equation}

    29	  197|   continuity on $0 \le s \le t \le T$. The map $D\mapsto U_D$ is locally
    30	  198|   Lipschitz into the uniform time-triangle norm, and
    31	  199|   \begin{equation}\label{E:constant-young-growth}
    32	  200|     \sup_{s\le t\le T}\|U_D(t,s)\|
    33	  201|     \le C_T\exp\big(C_T(1+\|D\|_{C^\theta})^{1/\theta}\big).

    44	  212|     +C_\theta[D]_\theta\ell^{2\theta}[V]_\theta,\\

    46	  214|     &\le[D]_\theta\sup\|V\|

    91	   30| \begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    92	   31|   \label{L:symplectic-free}
    93	   32|   There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    94	   33|   such that
    95	   34|   \[
    96	   35|     \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    97	   36|     =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    98	   37|     -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    99	   38|     \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
   100	   39|   \]
   101	   40|   The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
   102	   41|   $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
   103	   42| 
   104	   43|   Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
   105	   44|   zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
   106	   45|   \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
   107	   46|     U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
   108	   47|     \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
   109	   48|     \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
   110	   49|   \end{equation}
   111	   50|   More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
   112	   51|   and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
   113	   52|   Then
   114	   53|   \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
   115	   54|     P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
   116	   55|     \qquad
   117	   56|     \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
   118	   57|     \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
   119	   58|   \end{equation}
   120	   59|   These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
   121	   60| \end{lemma}
   122	   61| 
   123	   62| \begin{proof}
   124	   63|   The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
   125	   64|   onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
   126	   65|   $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
   127	   66|   operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
   128	   67|   displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
   129	   68|   of a general distributional velocity is taken.
   130	   69| 
   131	   70|   In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
   132	   71|   \[
   133	   72|     W_t(\xi)=
   134	   73|     \begin{pmatrix}
   135	   74|       \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
   136	   75|       -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
   137	   76|     \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
   138	   77|   \]
   139	   78|   At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
   140	   79|   the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
   141	   80|   $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
   142	   81|   $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
   143	   82|   bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
   144	   83|   Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
   145	   84|   Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
   146	   85|   Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
   147	   86|   generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
   148	   87| 
   149	   88|   Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
   150	   89|   Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
   151	   90|   $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
   152	   91|   Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
   153	   92|   Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
   154	   93|   proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
   155	   94|   $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
   156	   95|   \[
   157	   96|     \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
   158	   97|   \]
   159	   98|   is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
   160	   99|   of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   161	  100|   in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   162	  101|   that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   163	  102| 
   164	  103|   We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   165	  104|   Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   166	  105|   $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   167	  106|   transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   168	  107|   integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   169	  108|   function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by
   170	  109|   parts for the approximants, proves $\langle\tau_yz,w\rangle_E \to 0$ as $|y|
   171	  110|   \to \infty$. Thus, $\tau_yz$ tends weakly to zero. For compact $K$,
   172	  111|   $\|K\tau_yz\| \to 0$: otherwise compactness supplies a norm-convergent
   173	  112|   subsequence with nonzero norm, while bounded linear testing makes its limit
   174	  113|   zero. For unit $z$ it follows that
   175	  114|   \[
   176	  115|     \|S_E(h)+K\|
   177	  116|     \ge\liminf_{|y|\to\infty}\|(S_E(h)+K)\tau_yz\|
   178	  117|     \ge\|S_E(h)z\|.
   179	  118|   \]
   180	  119|   Taking the supremum over $z$ gives $\|S_E(h)+K\| \ge \|S_E(h)\|$. The
   181	  120|   isometric velocity reversal $\mathcal{R}(u,v) = (u,-v)$ satisfies $S_E(-h) =
   182	  121|   \mathcal{R} S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$ by the full free Fourier matrix. The group law
   183	  122|   yields $1 \le \|S_E(-h)\|\|S_E(h)\| = \|S_E(h)\|^2$. This
   184	  123|   proves~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}.
   185	  124| 
   186	  125|   Finally, $P_j-S_E(\ell_j)$ is compact. Telescoping the finite ordered product
   187	  126|   against its free product gives a finite sum of bounded--compact--bounded
   188	  127|   products, hence a compact difference. Only the free factors are combined by
   189	  128|   the group law; no noisy factors are commuted. The same translation argument
   190	  129|   proves \eqref{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}. A zero length gives $P_j
   191	  130|   = I$. All assertions are at fixed finite horizons and products; no uniform
   192	  131|   compact approximation in a radius, horizon or number of factors is asserted.
   193	  132|   This proves Lemma~\ref{L:symplectic-free}.
   194	  133| \end{proof}

  5618	Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
  5619	compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
  5620	`a284420` (statement lines 30-60, proof lines 62-133; all line numbers in
  5621	this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
  5622	`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
  5623	operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
  5624	the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
  5625	inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).
  5626	
  5627	What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
  5628	70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
  5629	quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
  5630	`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
  5631	frequency, zero included (lines 79-81), the per-frequency group law and the
  5632	reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 120-122). At nonzero frequency
  5633	the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
  5634	(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 40-41 and 88-91:
  5635	abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
  5636	(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
  5637	of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
  5638	`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
  5639	baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
  5640	left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
  5641	maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
  5642	`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
  5643	`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
  5644	`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 45-49) and
  5645	`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 53-58) in general form and as
  5646	exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
  5647	identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).
  5648	
  5649	Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
  5650	space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
  5651	group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
  5652	`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along

  5654	state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
  5655	the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
  5656	of lines 105-110). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for

     1	/-

     3	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.SymplecticFree.norm_le_norm_add_compact`
     4	(`‖S‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖` for compact `K`; `L:symplectic-free`,
     5	`notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` lines 103-119 at a284420).
     6	
     7	Wrong variant: the bound without the weakly null isometries commuting with `S`.
     8	Counterexample: on `ℝ`, `S = I` and the compact `K = -I` (finite rank) give
     9	`‖S + K‖ = 0 < 1 = ‖S‖`.  No contrast theorem: on `ℝ` there is no family of
    10	isometries that is weakly null along a nontrivial filter (every isometry is `±I`), so
    11	the package hypotheses cannot be met there; that hypothesis is what the
    12	counterexample shows to be needed.
    13	Junk-value reliance: none.
    14	
    15	Expected outcome: compiles (refuted).
    16	-/

    23	open Filter Topology

    25	/-- Auxiliary: `-I` is compact on `ℝ`. -/

    27	  refine ⟨Metric.closedBall 0 1, isCompact_closedBall 0 1, ?_⟩
    28	  have : (⇑(-1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ⁻¹' Metric.closedBall 0 1 = Metric.closedBall 0 1 := by
    29	    ext x; simp

    35	    ¬ (∀ S K : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ, IsCompactOperator (⇑K) → ‖S‖ ≤ ‖S + K‖) := by

   238	    E_{j+1}\le2E_j+2^{j+2}c_\theta\ell^\theta\delta B,\qquad
   239	    E_j\le2^jE_0+j2^{j+1}c_\theta\ell^\theta\delta B.
   240	  \]
   241	  Equation~\eqref{E:constant-young-difference} gives the same bound inside each
   242	  piece; a shorter final piece only reduces the coefficient. For evolutions,
   243	  $E_0 = 0$ and $B = 1$. The number of pieces is uniform in $s,t$, proving local
   244	  Lipschitz dependence in the full triangle norm.
   245	
   246	  Now choose $K = 1+\|D\|_{C^\theta}$. At most
   247	  $C_T(1+\|D\|_{C^\theta}^{1/\theta})$ pieces suffice. Each multiplies the norm
   248	  by at most two, giving \eqref{E:constant-young-growth}. Uniqueness patches the
   249	  solutions; right multiplication by the preceding evolution gives the
   250	  composition law. On a small piece~\eqref{E:constant-young-local} gives
   251	  $\|U_D-I\|_\infty \le 1/3$, so a Neumann series proves local invertibility,
   252	  then products give global invertibility. Finally, $U_D(t,s) =
   253	  U_D(t,0)U_D(s,0)^{-1}$ proves joint norm continuity, since $U_D(\cdot,0)$ is
   254	  continuous and inversion is continuous on invertible operators. This proves
   255	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear}.
   256	\end{proof}

   763	## DimensionalMatrix
   764	
   765	Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
   766	interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
   767	unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
   768	the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
   769	`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
   770	`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
   771	`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
   772	`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
   773	kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
   774	(`L:masked-continuous-wave`; defined in Lean as `MaskedContinuousWave.bFn`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
   775	change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
   776	`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
   777	zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
   778	are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
   779	`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in
   780	`L:symplectic-free`, which also defines the force `B(b)`.
   781	
   782	| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
   783	|---|---|---|---|
   784	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.backward` | Definition: `[[cp, -sp/p], [p sp, cp]]`, the backward free matrix `S(-t)` at one frequency. | The interpretation of `cp, sp` as cosine and sine of a phase, and the continuous extension at zero frequency. |
   785	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.coupling` | Definition: `[[0, 0], [H, 0]]`, the force `B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)` with `H` for `b`. | The meaning of `H` as a covariance coefficient. |
   786	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward` | Definition: `[[cq, sq/q], [-q sq, cq]]`, the free matrix `S(t)` at one frequency. | As for `backward`. |
   787	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.full_interaction` | For all real parameters (field division), `backward * coupling * forward = [[-(sp/p) H cq, -(sp/p) H (sq/q)], [cp H cq, cp H (sq/q)]]`, the unweighted product `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` at fixed frequencies. | The Bessel-weighted coordinate change and the weight `1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)` that turn it into `E:variance-normalized-kernel`; Fourier multiplication and covariance integrals; the zero-frequency case. |
   788

   137	\begin{lemma}[Ordinary response on all of $F$]\label{L:constant-source-response}
   138	  For fixed $\rho$ put $b(r) = mY_\rho(r)$ and define
   139	  \[
   140	    B_F(b)(e,c_1,c_2)=(0,b(e_1+c_1))\in E.
   141	  \]
   142	  Then
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:constant-source-response}
   144	    A_E^\rho(t)z=\int_0^tS(-r)B_F(b(r))S_F(r)z\ud r
   145	  \end{equation}
   146	  as a statewise strong integral. Its primitive is Lipschitz in
   147	  $\mathcal{B}(F,E)$ and the identity holds for all states and times on one
   148	  event for this fixed $\rho$.
   149	\end{lemma}
   150	
   151	\begin{proof}
   152	  The source regularity gives one compact spatial support for $b$, continuity in
   153	  $L^\infty$ and $L^2$, and bounded spatial derivatives on the horizon. Since
   154	  $e_1 \in L^2$ and $\|\cdot\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|\cdot\|_2$,
   155	  \[
   156	    \|B_F(b)\|_{\mathcal{B}(F,E)}
   157	    \le\|b\|_\infty+\|b\|_2.
   158	  \]
   159	  Strong continuity and finite-horizon bounds of both free groups make the
   160	  integrand strongly continuous on each state and uniformly bounded as an
   161	  operator. Integrating its bound proves operator-norm Lipschitz increments
   162	  without assuming a Banach-valued operator derivative.
   163	
   164	  The total initial distributions of $z$ and $iL_\psi z$ agree on the entire
   165	  enlarged ball where $\psi = 1$. Lemma~\ref{L:constant-phase-free} gives
   166	  equality of the free displacements near $\operatorname{supp}m$ for $0 \le r
   167	  \le T$. Multiplication by $b(r)$ kills the difference. Apply
   168	  Proposition~\ref{P:source-ordinary-response} to the $E$ state $L_\psi z$ to
   169	  obtain~\eqref{E:constant-source-response}. Separability and rational times,
   170	  followed by boundedness and continuity, give its path identity. This proves
   171	  the constant columns directly; no density of $E$ in $F$ is used. This proves
   172	  Lemma~\ref{L:constant-source-response}.
   173	\end{proof}

   175	\subsection{The exact linear Young equation}
   176	
   177	We use Young's integration theory~\cite{young:36:inequality} in its
   178	Banach-space form. The estimate is stated by
   179	Friz and Hairer~\cite{friz.hairer:20:course}*{Sections~1.4--1.5, 4.1, (4.3), pp.~13, 61--62}.
   180	For $D,V$ with exponent $\theta > 1/2$ and bounded bilinear multiplication, left
   181	composition gives
   182	\begin{equation}\label{E:constant-young-estimate}
   183	  \left\|\int_s^t\ud D(r)V(r)-D(s,t)V(s)\right\|
   184	  \le C_\theta[D]_\theta[V]_\theta|t-s|^{2\theta}.
   185	\end{equation}
   186	The Banach spaces here are $\mathcal{B}(F)$, and multiplication is bounded with
   187	constant one. We derive the linear solution and stability estimates below rather
   188	than invoke a nonlinear bounded-vector-field theorem.
   189
